messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: SLO violation detected on staging-hostpool-3 (shared-gpu). p95 latency > 500ms and p99 > 1.2s for streaming endpoints (model: redwood-7b-v1). Streaming stalls increased by 7x in last 5m. Auto-escalation -> incidents channel.

oncall-amber: acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking traces. starting triage.

maria-eng: seeing heavy iowait on hostpool-3 nodes, top shows writeback spikes, cgroups for tenant t-42 near blkio limit. KV cache hitrate dropping ~40%.

sahil-sre: can you paste the iostat / dstat snapshot? also any recent deploys to that pool?

maria-eng: pasted logs:
```
2024-06-06T18:07:03 hostpool-3 kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 1234567
2024-06-06T18:07:04 hostpool-3 cgroup_blkio: t-42 write_bytes 524288000
2024-06-06T18:07:05 hostpool-3 kv-cache: eviction=1200 entries, behindload=85%
```

oncall-amber: no recent deploys. usage spike appears tenant-driven. p95 for streaming route /v1/stream now 630ms, p99 1.25s (from observability).

kevin-ml: model backend reports many small-sequence requests causing frequent KV cache churn and high NVMe IO. t-42 is running a beam search reranking job with many short calls.

ops-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/noisy-tenant-mitigation (automated)

oncall-amber: immediate mitigations: 1) throttle t-42 at routing layer to cap concurrency to 8; 2) temporarily pin heavy requests to dedicated-worker-7 (if capacity); 3) increase blkio weight for system processes to prioritize host background IO. Doing 1 now.

maria-eng: throttling rule applied for tenant t-42 -> concurrency cap 8. routing shows immediate drop in in-flight requests from 260 -> 90.

sahil-sre: monitoring kernel writeback and nvme queues. initial writeback dropped ~60% after throttle. p95 trending down. good sign.

oncall-amber: notify support & product about customer impact. helena please post to affected-customers thread with estimated ETA.

helena-support: posting now. message: "We've detected latency spikes affecting streaming inferences for some customers. We've applied traffic caps to reduce impact; we expect recovery within 15-30m. We'll follow up with postmortem."

ryan-product: which customers behind t-42? any paid customers impacted?

maria-eng: t-42 is a mid-market partner on staging-like pool (not prod), but had cross-tenant traffic routed here due to autoscaler placement. No direct high-tier prod customers impacted, but we will run post-incident audit.

kevin-ml: long-term: recommend request batching adjustments + KV cache TTL tuning for short-sequence workloads. Also consider tenant-aware placement to keep heavy KV churn off shared nvme pools.

oncall-amber: live mitigation checklist: (a) traffic cap active, (b) moving evicted tenant to dedicated worker in progress, (c) alert thresholds tightened for blkio and kv eviction.

ops-bot: migration job started -> move t-42 workloads to dedicated-worker-7 (estimated 4 nodes).

sahil-sre: re-checking SLO numbers: p95 now 290ms, p99 520ms for streaming route. Still slightly above baseline but within tolerance for staged SLA.

oncall-amber: leaving a handoff note for followup oncall in 30m. tagging @oncall-night. please pick up if regressions appear.

maria-eng: post-action: increased KV cache TTL from 15s -> 60s for that tenant pattern, disabled aggressive eviction for 10m window during migration. logging applied.

helena-support: customer update sent. one partner confirmed reduced errors.

kevin-ml: opened task INF-7234 to evaluate tenant-aware scheduling and cgroup adjustments for shared nvme pools.

oncall-amber: summary for postmortem: root cause = noisy-tenant IO churn causing KV cache eviction + host nvme saturation; immediate mitigations = traffic cap, tenant migration, KV TTL tweak; impact = elevated p95/p99 for streaming endpoints, staging partner affected; follow-ups = tenant-aware placement, TTL/eviction tuning, tighter blkio telemetry.

ops-bot: automated incident closed when p99 < 600ms for 10m. Closing thread now, postmortem to be scheduled. :white_check_mark:
